name: Butternut Squash "Brownies" with Almond Butter, Oat Flour & Maple Syrup

instructions.primary_message: Wash, dry, trim, and peel squash; halve lengthwise, scrape out the seeds, and medium dice. Place squash in a medium saucepan and cover with hot water (from the tap). Cover and bring to a boil over high heat; once boiling, reduce to a simmer and cook until soft, about 12 minutes.

Meanwhile, preheat oven to 350°F. Coat the bottom and sides of an 8-inch square cake pan or baking dish with cooking spray. Cut a piece of parchment paper to fit the bottom and press down into the dish. Set aside.
When the squash is done, drain in a colander and return to the pan; using a potato masher, mash until smooth and creamy. Set aside to cool, 10 minutes.

While the squash is cooling, place maple syrup, almond butter, cocoa powder, oat flour, almond flour, oil, vanilla, baking powder, baking soda, cinnamon, and salt in a medium bowl. Whisk to combine the batter.
instructions.secondary_message:
½ cup pure maple syrup
½ cup natural almond butter
½ cup cocoa powder
½ cup oat flour
⅓ cup almond meal/flour
2 tbsp neutral vegetable oil
1 tsp vanilla extract
1 tsp baking powder
½ tsp baking soda
½ tsp cinnamon, ground
½ tsp salt

instructions.primary_message: Once the butternut mash has cooled, measure out 1 1/2 cups and add to the bowl with the batter. Whisk once more to combine. (Reserve any remaining mash for another use.)

Transfer batter to the cake pan and gently spread out in an even layer. Place pan in the oven and bake until brownies are just set, 25-30 minutes (when the brownies are done, the center may still appear slightly underbaked; it will firm up slightly as it cools). Remove from oven and let cool until just warm to the touch, 20-30 minutes.
Once the brownies have cooled slightly, remove from the pan, cut into squares, and arrange on a serving platter. Best enjoyed warm!
